fixes.find: A share's price can change only once a minute, and most of those changes come from traders, not from the company.
fixes.replace: A share's price can change many times a minute, and those changes come from buyers and sellers, not from the company.
fixes.why: Prices change continuously during trading hours, not once a minute.

fixes.find: Big Indian companies are cut into exactly 1,000 pieces, so 1 share is like one grain from a full rice godown.
fixes.replace: Big Indian companies are cut into millions or even billions of pieces, so 1 share is like one grain from a full rice godown.
fixes.why: There is no fixed 1,000 pieces; big listed companies have far more shares.

fixes.find: with a guaranteed share of the profits every month and a vote at the yearly meeting.
fixes.replace: with a claim on a share of the company's profits (paid as dividends, which are not guaranteed) and a vote at the yearly meeting.
fixes.why: Profits are not guaranteed or paid monthly.

fixes.find: From then on, you usually buy your slice directly from the company, not from another owner.
fixes.replace: From then on, you usually buy your slice from another owner, not from the company.
fixes.why: After the first sale, trading happens between investors.

fixes.find: Benjamin Graham, who was taught by Warren Buffett,
fixes.replace: Benjamin Graham, who taught Warren Buffett,
fixes.why: Roles reversed: Graham was Buffett's teacher.
Price rises when buyers outnumber sellers; the company doesn't set it.

fixes.find: Buyers and sellers don't set the price; the company does.
fixes.replace: The company doesn't set the daily price; it is formed by trading.
fixes.why: Original whyNot was for the wrong option and false; reworded for option a's logic.

fixes.find: India's oldest exchange, the Bombay Stock Exchange, opened in 1995.
fixes.replace: exchanges such as the Bombay Stock Exchange (founded in 1875) and the National Stock Exchange.

fixes.find: 4 hands up and 40 slices on offer, and it falls. News
fixes.replace: 4 hands up and 40 slices on offer, and it falls. In the first case it rises. News
fixes.why: With 40 buyers for 4 slices the price rises, not falls.
